findings.source: hMath.sol:14 rpow: for { n := div(n, 2) } n { n := div(n,2) } { let xx := mul(x, x) ... x := div(xxRound, b) if mod(n,2) { ... z := div(zxRound, b) } }
findings.issue: The Yul loop is found and correct (the x == 0 case even folds to the Panic(17) of the later subtraction), but ONE = 10^27 and half prints as 1000000000 * 10**18 and 500000000 * 10**18, the new x is computed twice instead of once, and the helper SafeMath.mul(a, b) checks 'a * b / a == a', an overflow test only valid for its single use mul(u, u).
findings.rule: Print 10^k (and 5 * 10^k) as such; name a value computed once and used twice (x := (xx + half) / b) at its computation; specialise helper names to the check they make (a squaring check) or keep the general form b == a * b / a.

notes: 69 ABI functions; the long ones (deposit, withdraw(For), borrow, payback(For), auctions, currentLiquidationPrice, willBorrow) read by structure, the rest in full. Source loops in this bytecode: addToWhitelist (676), removeFromWhitelist (715), addToAuctionWhitelist (637), removeFromAuctionWhitelist (598), addToBlacklist (559), removeFromBlacklist (524), hMath.rpow (borrowApr 439); all while. AuctionProxy.getAllActiveAuctionsForClip, listed by the pack, runs in the linked library (delegate 0x11e9..3d3a.unknown7ce53fed) and is not counted; the two loops of getAllActiveAuctionsForToken decode and re-encode the returned Sale[] (implicit, P7). P9: the FullMath-style mulmod arithmetic of collateralTVL/currentLiquidationPrice (42 mulmod lines). Storage naming is good where getters exist (wards, collaterals, whitelist...).
summary: A faithful text in which all seven loops of this bytecode are found (including the Yul rpow loop); the usual raw buffers after the first call, 10^27 printed as 10^9 * 10^18 and a few recomputed or oddly specialised helpers are the main readability costs.
